description: LIGHT MULTI-TURN Biomni task: a full scanpy scRNA-seq pipeline on PBMC 3k (QC -> normalize -> HVG -> PCA -> neighbors -> UMAP -> Leiden clustering -> Wilcoxon marker genes -> cell-type annotation). Many small CPU tool phases (historically 19-32 turns) = the 'light multi-turn' resource type for the benchmark, contrasting the single-big-phase CPU tasks.
prompt: Perform a complete single-cell RNA-seq analysis of the PBMC 3k dataset using scanpy (already installed). Load the dataset with scanpy.datasets.pbmc3k(), run standard quality control (filter low-quality cells and lowly expressed genes, remove high-mitochondrial-content cells), normalize and log-transform the data, select highly variable genes, run PCA, build a neighbor graph, compute UMAP, perform Leiden clustering at resolution 0.5, and identify the top 5 marker genes per cluster using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Annotate each cluster with its most likely PBMC cell type based on canonical marker genes (e.g. CD3D/CD3E for T cells, MS4A1/CD79A for B cells, LYZ/CST3 for monocytes, GNLY/NKG7 for NK cells). Report the final number of cells after QC, the number of clusters, each cluster's size, and its cell type annotation.
notes: Re-validated into the trusted set 2026-08-17 (was in tasks/_deprecated_fake/). LIGHT multi-turn CPU type for the benchmark. Deps scanpy/leidenalg/igraph installed in biomni-sglang (2026-06-22). DATA: scanpy.datasets.pbmc3k() DOWNLOADS ~6MB on first load then caches -> works on du04 (has internet); on MN5 (NO internet on compute/login nodes) the pbmc3k cache must be pre-staged before running. success_markers are a FIRST GUESS (numeric cluster + cell counts = results, not prompt phrases) -- expect to tune after the first run, exactly like bindingdb needed 2 iterations. Historically 19-32 turns, ~8.8% bubble, mixed cpu/gpu/trivial phases (some scanpy ops touched the GPU).
